speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I'm Dr. Agent. To help me understand your condition, can you describe the appearance of the rash in more detail, such as whether it consists of raised bumps, blisters, or flat red patches? Also, when did the rash first appear relative to your fever and other symptoms?

speaker: Patient
text: 11-year-old girl. The patient has been experiencing a mildly pruritic rash on her trunk and extremities for 2 days. One week ago, she developed symptoms of low-grade fever, rhinorrhea, and headache. A facial rash appeared 4 days later, sparing the perioral area.

speaker: Doctor
text: Does the rash on her trunk and extremities resemble a "slapped cheek" appearance, and has it spread to her arms and legs in a lacy or reticular pattern? I will also check for any joint pain or swelling, as this is common in this condition. REQUEST IMAGES

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Mildly pruritic rash on trunk and extremities. I also have Low-grade fever, Rhinorrhea, Headache, Facial rash not involving the perioral skin.

speaker: Doctor
text: The clinical presentation of a facial rash sparing the perioral area followed by a lacy, reticular rash on the trunk and extremities is classic for Erythema Infectiosum, also known as Fifth Disease. DIAGNOSIS READY: Erythema Infectiosum (Fifth Disease)
